criteriaNotes.1_topdown_view: Marginal pass. Top face (rows 4-16) and south front face (rows 17-27) exist and there are no iso side faces, but the top/front edge is not stated: the only bright ridge is row 16 x=10-16 under the window plus a seam line of j on row 12; across x=17-45 the transition from top to front is just mid-grey noise, so the mass reads as one slanted lump rather than a lid on a body.
criteriaNotes.2_style_fit: Pass with notes. 14 opaque colours + 1 shadow (12,10,8,a110) — acceptable, r1's 26-colour mess is fixed. Ramp steps a/f/i/e/c/d/b/j are each ~25-30 apart, no near-duplicates; k (40,36,32) sits close to a (30,44,50) but is a warm accent, tolerable. Dark outline matches the surrounding trees/stones. Shadow is one flat semi-alpha colour on the SE only, no fringe.
criteriaNotes.3_readability_1x: FAIL. At 1x and in context_x3 it reads as a grey hexagonal boulder / stone slab with a blue water basin, not a silver star-metal pod. Causes: (a) the body fill is broken horizontal dashes of d/f/i/e over c — that is stone grain/masonry texture, not brushed metal; (b) no continuous specular streak along the length, so no metallic read; (c) the window (g/m with 2 px h glint) reads as a puddle in a trough; (d) the glowing crack is only 2 px of l at (38,13),(39,14) — invisible in context; (e) the 6 k 'rivets' are isolated dark pits that look like stone holes; (f) no scorch visible. The r2 'stone slab' rejection is NOT fixed.
criteriaNotes.4_placement: Pass. Sits inside the crater floor, shadow falls SE consistently, 48x32 vs ~16x24 hero is a plausible coffin size. No impact ring/scorch decal under it, but that is a map concern not an object fail.
criteriaNotes.5_silhouette_outline: FAIL. Both ends are flat vertical walls: foot end x=45 is a straight 17-px vertical (y=10..26), head end x=0 a 12-px vertical (y=12..23). Result is an elongated hexagon, not a coffin taper (r1 'square foot end' persists). The 'widest at head shoulder' point is not expressed — the top edge just slopes monotonically from y=4 (x13) to y=10 (x45). No orphan pixels and no opaque fringe (r2 fringe fixed).

items.name: 떨어진 별의 관
items.reasons: Reads as a grey hexagonal stone slab with a water basin, not a silver coffin-pod (r2 rejection not fixed); square vertical ends on both sides (foot x=45 straight for 17 rows). Fixes: (1) Silhouette: replace the vertical end columns with a coffin outline — shoulder bulge at x~12-16 (tallest/widest), then taper to a 4-6 px rounded point at the foot (x=44-46 covering only y~15..21) and a shorter 6-8 px rounded head cap at x=0-2; step the outline in 1-2 px runs so no straight run exceeds ~5 px. (2) Separate lid from body: draw a continuous 1-px j/b rim highlight along the whole top/front edge (follow the coffin outline ~5-6 px below the top), and a 1-px a/f shadow line directly under it, so the top face (lid) and the south front face (side band) are unmistakable. (3) Metal, not stone: remove all the scattered d/f/i dashes in the body; fill the lid with smooth c with one long j specular streak running the length (2-3 px wide near the shoulder, thinning to 1 px toward the foot), and fill the front band with flat e/i vertical-banded shading, darkest at the bottom. (4) Rivets: put k/f rivets in a regular row along the rim (every 4-5 px) with a 1-px b highlight above each, instead of random pits. (5) Crack: make the glowing crack a visible 5-8 px zig-zag of l with h core across the lid near the foot, flanked by 1 px m. (6) Window: give it a 1-px j frame ring and a 2-3 px diagonal h glint so it reads as glass, and keep it inset at the shoulder. (7) Scorch: add 4-8 px of warm-dark k soot smudge on the front band at the foot end. Re-hash and re-judge after redraw.
